title: HSBC's FCNR Strategy & GIFT City: A New Pull for NRIs
description: HSBC is actively leveraging FCNR (Foreign Currency Non-Resident) deposits to attract Non-Resident Indian (NRI) funds. FCNR deposits allow NRIs to hold savings.

faq.q: What is the minimum tenure for an FCNR deposit?
faq.a: The minimum tenure for an FCNR (B) deposit is typically one year. The maximum tenure can go up to five years, though specific banks might offer different ranges.

faq.q: Is the interest earned on FCNR deposits taxable in India for NRIs?
faq.a: No, the interest earned on FCNR (B) deposits is fully exempt from income tax in India for Non-Resident Indians. However, you may have tax obligations in your country of residence.

faq.q: Can I open an FCNR deposit in any foreign currency?
faq.a: FCNR deposits are generally offered in major freely convertible currencies like USD, GBP, EUR, JPY, and CAD. The specific currencies available may vary by bank.

faq.q: What is the difference between an NRE account and an FCNR deposit?
faq.a: An NRE (Non-Resident External) account is denominated in Indian Rupees, meaning your foreign currency is converted to INR upon deposit. An FCNR deposit, however, is held in a foreign currency, protecting it from Rupee depreciation. Both are fully repatriable.

Deposits in FCNR accounts with scheduled commercial banks are covered by the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) for up to ₹5 lakhs per depositor per bank, similar to other eligible deposits.

faq.q: How does GIFT City benefit NRIs specifically?
faq.a: GIFT City offers a liberalised regulatory environment, tax incentives (like certain income tax exemptions for entities and GST exemptions), and a platform for diverse international financial products, allowing NRIs to invest and manage wealth through an internationally aligned hub.

faq.q: Can I take a loan against my FCNR deposit?
faq.a: Yes, you can avail a loan against your FCNR (B) deposit, either in India or abroad, from the bank holding the deposit or another financial institution, subject to their terms and conditions.
